references.text: God repeats his promise to Isaac with reference to the oath he swore to Abraham and blesses him because of Abraham's obedience.
The promise that all peoples on earth will be blessed through Abraham's offspring, given as a direct result of his obedience and willingness to sacrifice Isaac.
Hebrews points out that God swore by himself when he gave the promise to Abraham, because there was no one greater to swear by—a direct reference to Gen 22:16.
Hebrews mentions Abraham's faith when he was tested and willing to offer up Isaac, the event that triggered God's oath in Gen 22:16.
James refers to Abraham's justification by works when he offered his son Isaac on the altar, which is the context for God's oath in Gen 22:16.
God swears by himself—a parallel to the words 'by myself I have sworn' in Gen 22:16.
Zechariah's song of praise refers to the oath God swore to Abraham, which originates from Gen 22:16.
Hebrews interprets Abraham's action in Genesis as an expression of faith, thereby confirming the theological weight of God's oath.
